hints.dec.place-value.read: After the point the places go tenths, hundredths, thousandths. The bottom number tells you which place the last digit goes in.
hints.dec.place-value.compare: Write zeros on the end so both have the same number of places (0.5 = 0.50). Then compare.
hints.dec.place-value.round: Look at the digit just after the place you're rounding to. 5 or more: round up. Less than 5: keep it.
hints.dec.place-value: Tenths, hundredths, thousandths. To compare, give both the same number of places. To round, look at the next digit.

misconceptionMessages.dec.place-value-shift: Check the places: tenths are the first place after the point, hundredths the second. 7/100 is 7 hundredths: 0.07.
misconceptionMessages.dec.longer-is-larger: More digits doesn't mean bigger. Write both with the same number of places: 0.5 = 0.50, and 50 hundredths is more than 45 hundredths.
misconceptionMessages.dec.shorter-is-larger: Write both with the same number of places and compare: 0.4 = 0.40, which is less than 0.45.
misconceptionMessages.dec.round-truncate: Rounding isn't just cutting digits off. Look at the next digit: if it's 5 or more, round up.
misconceptionMessages.dec.round-wrong-way: Look at the digit just after the place you're rounding to: 5 or more rounds up, less than 5 stays.
misconceptionMessages.dec.round-wrong-place: Check which place the question asks for: nearest whole number, tenth, or hundredth.

sections.title: Tenths, hundredths, thousandths
sections.objective: Write fractions with 10, 100, 1000 as decimals, and name the place of a digit.
explain: Each place is 10 times smaller than the one to its left. The point sits between the ones and the tenths.
The bottom of the fraction says which place the last digit goes in. Fill any empty places with 0.

visual.caption: 3.45 in a place-value chart. Each column is 10 times the column to its right.

sections.key: After the point: tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths. 7/100 is 7 hundredths, so the 7 goes in the second place: 0.07.

worked.note: the 7 goes in the hundredths place; 0 fills the tenths

sections.title: Compare decimals
sections.objective: Compare decimals, even when they have different numbers of digits.
explain: Compare the whole-number parts first. If they're the same, write zeros on the end so both have the same number of places.
Zeros on the end don't change a decimal: 0.5 and 0.50 are the same amount.
sections.key: More digits doesn't mean bigger. Give both decimals the same number of places, then compare them like whole numbers.

worked.note: write a zero on the end

sections.workedCaption: Tap through and compare the two grids.

sections.title: Round decimals
sections.objective: Round to the nearest whole number, tenth, or hundredth.
explain: Find the place you're rounding to, then look at the digit just after it.
5 or more: round up. Less than 5: the digit stays. Then drop the digits after it.
sections.key: Look at the digit just after the place you're rounding to. 5 or more rounds up; less than 5 stays the same.
